author: curriculum-architect
songSummary: Practices finding keys by landmarks, mirror patterns, counting beats and the song's shape, while you and your child play Ode to Joy together.

classes.title: Find your five-finger house
classes.goal: Hear the whole song and find C, the door of your five-finger house.

mathTarget.parentLine: Using the two black keys as a sign to find C

classes.parentPrompt: Point to the two black keys, then help your child rest the thumb on C.
classes.childAction: Find the two black keys, then put your thumb on C.
classes.bridge: Two black keys are a roof; C is the door just left of it.

intro.caption: Find the two black keys
intro.parentCue: C is the door just to their left

games.caption: One finger, one key
games.parentCue: Say the finger number for each key

classes.celebrate: Today you practiced: finding C and one finger per key.

classes.title: Up the stairs, down again
classes.goal: Play the first lines and feel how the tune climbs up and comes back down.

mathTarget.parentLine: The tune goes up three steps, then back down the same steps

classes.parentPrompt: Walk two fingers up your child's arm on the way up, then back down.
classes.childAction: Fingers three, four, five climb up, then five, four, three come down.
classes.bridge: Each key is a stair: step up to G, then step back down.

intro.caption: Up the stairs, down the stairs
intro.parentCue: Walk your fingers up and down the arm

games.caption: Climb up, climb down
games.parentCue: Say three, four, five, five, four, three

classes.celebrate: Today you practiced: a mirror pattern, up and back down.

classes.title: Which line goes home?
classes.goal: Learn the next lines and hear which ending lands back home on C.

mathTarget.parentLine: Two lines start the same; only one ends on home C

classes.parentPrompt: After each line, ask: did it land home? Cheer with a hug when it does.
classes.childAction: Listen to the ending and pat your lap when it lands on C.
classes.bridge: C is the front door: the last note walks right back inside.

intro.caption: Is the song home yet?
intro.parentCue: Ask your child after each line

games.caption: Which one goes home?
games.parentCue: Pat your lap together on the home note

classes.celebrate: Today you practiced: hearing same and different endings.

classes.title: Little steps, big frog hop
classes.goal: Learn the dance line, with small steps and one big hop down to low G.

mathTarget.parentLine: Notes next door are steps; the far low note is a hop

classes.parentPrompt: Show your child the low G outside the house, then help the thumb hop there.
classes.childAction: Tiptoe the small steps, then hop your thumb down to low G.
classes.bridge: Steps are next-door keys; the frog hop jumps far left, where sounds are low.

intro.caption: Small steps, then a frog hop
intro.parentCue: Hop your hand down on your lap

games.caption: Tiny steps, then hop!
games.parentCue: Hop your hands down on the big jump

classes.celebrate: Today you practiced: small steps, a big leap, low on the left.

classes.title: Spot the happy tune
classes.goal: Play the whole song slowly and count how many times the happy tune returns.

mathTarget.parentLine: One tune comes back three times, like a chorus

classes.parentPrompt: Each time 'Happy, happy' starts, hold up one more finger and count aloud.
classes.childAction: Play slowly and say the number each time the happy tune returns.
classes.bridge: The happy tune is a friend who visits three times; wave hello each time.

intro.caption: Count the happy tune
intro.parentCue: hold up a finger each time it returns

games.caption: Tap the beat: the first line
games.parentCue: Play the blue keys; your child taps the beat

classes.celebrate: Today you practiced: the song's shape and counting the repeats.

classes.title: Walk, walk, run-ning
classes.goal: Practise the bouncy dance lines slowly, where two quick notes share one beat.

mathTarget.parentLine: Two quick notes fit in the time of one walking note

classes.parentPrompt: Say 'walk' for long notes and 'run-ning' for the two quick ones.
classes.childAction: Say walk and run-ning while your fingers play the dance line.
classes.bridge: A walking note is one big step; run-ning is two tiny mouse steps.

intro.caption: Walk and run-ning
intro.parentCue: Say the words with every note

games.caption: Walk, run-ning, walk, walk
games.parentCue: Say the words slowly with each key

classes.celebrate: Today you practiced: two quick notes in one beat.

classes.title: Four beats, slow and even
classes.goal: Play the whole song slowly and evenly, feeling four beats in every bar.

mathTarget.parentLine: Beats come in groups of four, again and again

classes.parentPrompt: Tap your child's shoulder on each beat and count 1, 2, 3, 4 softly.
classes.childAction: Play slowly and evenly while you count to four together.
classes.bridge: Each bar is a little train with four cars: one, two, three, four.
classes.celebrate: Today you practiced: steady beats in groups of four.

classes.title: Keep up with the band
classes.goal: Play the whole song along with the music and keep going, even after a slip.

mathTarget.parentLine: Matching your playing to the speed of the music

classes.parentPrompt: Sing the words along and nod on each beat; if a note slips, keep going.
classes.childAction: Play with the music and keep going, like a train on its track.
classes.bridge: The music is a moving train; hop on and ride, even past bumps.

intro.caption: Hop on the music train
intro.parentCue: Sing along and keep the beat

classes.celebrate: Today you practiced: keeping pace with the music together.

classes.title: Concert for teddy
classes.goal: Play the whole song from start to end for a teddy, then bow and celebrate.

mathTarget.parentLine: Knowing what comes first, next and last in the song

classes.parentPrompt: Sit teddy as the audience; announce the song, then clap and bow together at the end.
classes.childAction: Bow, play the whole song for teddy, then bow again.
classes.bridge: Play it like a happy parade: proud start, bouncy middle, home at the end.
classes.celebrate: Today you practiced: playing start to end, and sharing music.
